status: proposed; outcomes and tiers are curator hypotheses to verify by reading the adjudicating passages, not labels
evaluator_only: Contains outcomes. Never place in candidate context.

original.label: Havlicek et al. 2019, quantum-enhanced feature spaces

candidates.claim: Kernels from feature maps that are hard to estimate classically can give a classification advantage on suitable data.

adjudicators.label: Thanasilp et al., exponential concentration in quantum kernel methods
Shaydulin & Wild, importance of kernel bandwidth

candidates.notes: Hardware demo on a synthetic dataset; the advantage claim is conjectural in the paper itself. Test whether the verdict separates the demonstration from the advantage claim.

original.label: Cong, Choi, Lukin 2019, quantum convolutional neural networks

candidates.claim: QCNNs recognize quantum phases with sample complexity beyond existing approaches, using a circuit with O(log N) parameters.

adjudicators.label: Bermejo et al., QCNNs are effectively classically simulable

candidates.notes: Simulability holds for the locally easy, low-bodyness regimes studied; quantum data acquisition may still be needed. Score the exact claim.

original.label: Kerenidis & Prakash 2016, quantum recommendation systems

candidates.claim: An exponential speedup over classical algorithms for recommendation, given QRAM-style data access.

adjudicators.label: Tang, quantum-inspired classical algorithm for recommendation systems

candidates.notes: Algorithm correctness survives; the exponential separation does not under comparable sampling access. Overlaps synthetic eval5.

original.label: Lloyd, Mohseni, Rebentrost 2014, quantum principal component analysis

candidates.claim: Exponential speedup for principal component analysis of an unknown low-rank density matrix.

adjudicators.label: Tang, QPCA only achieves an exponential speedup because of its state preparation assumptions

candidates.notes: Speedup on classical data is dequantized; the quantum-data-input setting is a different access model. Good scope test.

original.label: Perez-Salinas et al. 2020, data re-uploading for a universal quantum classifier

candidates.claim: A single-qubit re-uploading classifier is universal and performs competitively on benchmark classification tasks.

adjudicators.label: Bowles, Ahmed, Schuld, better than classical? benchmarking QML models

candidates.notes: Universality is formal and survives; competitiveness against tuned classical baselines is the adjudicated part. Confirm the benchmark includes this model.

original.label: Huang et al. 2021, power of data in quantum machine learning

candidates.claim: Projected quantum kernels outperform classical models on datasets engineered to have a large geometric difference.

adjudicators.label: Bowles, Ahmed, Schuld, better than classical? benchmarking QML models

candidates.notes: Positive case within an engineered-data scope. Confirm what the benchmark says about projected kernels before assigning a tier.

original.label: Liu, Arunachalam, Temme 2021, rigorous and robust quantum speed-up in supervised learning

candidates.claim: A quantum kernel learner achieves an end-to-end speedup on a discrete-log-based classification task, under standard hardness assumptions.
candidates.notes: Formal positive control. No external adjudication identified yet; tier C until one is found. Mining found discussion (e.g. 2406.07072 on trainability vs dequantization) but no claim-level adjudication. Formal positive control; tier C unless an independent proof check is found.

original.label: McClean et al. 2018, barren plateaus in quantum neural network training landscapes

candidates.claim: Gradients of sufficiently random parameterized circuits vanish exponentially in the number of qubits.

adjudicators.label: Cerezo et al., cost function dependent barren plateaus
Larocca et al., review of barren plateaus

candidates.notes: Cerezo et al. is independent of the original authors; the 2024 review includes McClean and does not count toward independence.

original.label: Arute et al. 2019, quantum supremacy using a programmable superconducting processor

candidates.claim: Sampling the 53-qubit random circuits at the reported fidelity would take a state-of-the-art supercomputer about 10,000 years.

adjudicators.label: Pan, Chen, Zhang, solving the sampling problem of the Sycamore quantum circuits

candidates.notes: The classical-cost estimate is refuted; the hardware fidelity results stand. Claim-level split. arXiv 1910.11333 is the supplementary information, not the paper; use the Nature DOI.

original.label: Kim et al. 2023, evidence for the utility of quantum computing before fault tolerance

candidates.claim: Error-mitigated expectation values for a 127-qubit kicked Ising circuit are accurate in regimes beyond brute-force classical simulation.

adjudicators.label: Tindall et al., efficient tensor network simulation of IBM's Eagle kicked Ising experiment
Begusic & Chan, fast classical simulation of evidence for the utility of quantum computing

candidates.notes: Error-mitigation accuracy survives; beyond-classical framing does not in the reported regime. Begusic & Chan citation not found in Semantic Scholar or OpenAlex reference lists; the paper's subject is this experiment, so treat as an index gap and confirm in the PDF.

original.label: Zhong et al. 2020, quantum computational advantage using photons (Jiuzhang)

candidates.claim: Gaussian boson sampling with 76 detected photons is infeasible to reproduce classically at the reported rate.

adjudicators.label: Villalonga et al., efficient approximation of experimental Gaussian boson sampling

candidates.notes: Rebuttal spoofs the benchmark tests used; exact sampling hardness is not refuted. Claim-level. Author-overlap flag 'L. Li' is a name collision (Google vs USTC), not shared authorship.

original.label: King et al. 2025, beyond-classical computation in quantum simulation (D-Wave)

candidates.claim: Quantum annealer dynamics of spin glasses are beyond the reach of classical simulation methods at the reported accuracy.

adjudicators.label: Tindall et al., dynamics of disordered quantum systems with 2D tensor networks
Mauron & Carleo, challenging the quantum advantage frontier with large-scale classical simulations of annealing dynamics

candidates.notes: Live dispute with replies; good test that the verdict stays INCONCLUSIVE rather than picking a side. Mauron & Carleo citation not found in either index; confirm in the PDF.

original.label: Denchev et al. 2016, what is the computational value of finite-range tunneling?

candidates.claim: The D-Wave 2X is about 10^8 times faster than simulated annealing on crafted instances.

adjudicators.label: Mandra et al., strengths and weaknesses of weak-strong cluster problems

candidates.notes: Speedup holds against simulated annealing; not against the strongest classical solvers. Weak-baseline lesson, directly relevant to criterion 5.

original.label: Harrow, Hassidim, Lloyd 2009, quantum algorithm for linear systems of equations

candidates.claim: Exponential speedup for solving sparse, well-conditioned linear systems, returning a quantum state.

adjudicators.label: Aaronson, read the fine print

candidates.notes: Algorithm stands; end-to-end advantage depends on input/output caveats. Matches the deprioritized-HHL rule in CLAUDE.md.

original.label: Zhang et al. 2018, quantized Majorana conductance (retracted 2021)

candidates.claim: A zero-bias conductance plateau at 2e^2/h is evidence of Majorana zero modes.

adjudicators.label: Retraction note: Quantized Majorana conductance
Yu et al., non-Majorana states yield nearly quantized conductance

candidates.notes: Retracted after data-selection issues. Verify the retraction notice DOI. The retraction note is by the original authors (self-retraction): authoritative for the claim's evidential status but not an independent replication. Yu et al. shares Bakkers (device growth). Confirm whether independent critics (e.g. published data-selection concerns) triggered the retraction before assigning tier A.

original.label: Lee et al. 2023, LK-99 room-temperature ambient-pressure superconductor

candidates.claim: Cu-doped lead apatite is a superconductor at room temperature and ambient pressure.
candidates.notes: Multiple independent replications attributed effects to Cu2S impurities. Adjudicator IDs to be found by citation mining. Citation mining found no challenger: Semantic Scholar has few citation passages for this preprint. Find replication papers manually (independent synthesis attributing the transition to Cu2S).

original.label: Carleo & Troyer 2017, solving the quantum many-body problem with artificial neural networks

candidates.claim: Neural-network quantum states reach state-of-the-art variational accuracy for ground states of 1D/2D spin models.

adjudicators.label: Wu et al., variational benchmarks for quantum many-body problems

candidates.notes: Positive physics case. Benchmark compares many variational methods; check what it says about NQS accuracy in the original models. Variational benchmarks paper includes Carleo as co-author: not independent, so tier B at most unless an unrelated benchmark is found.

original.label: He et al. 2017, neural collaborative filtering

candidates.claim: An MLP-based interaction function outperforms the dot product of matrix factorization for implicit-feedback recommendation.

adjudicators.label: Rendle et al., neural collaborative filtering vs. matrix factorization revisited
Ferrari Dacrema et al., are we really making much progress?

candidates.notes: Weak-baseline case: a properly tuned dot product beats the MLP. Relevant to the lab's recsys experiments.

original.label: Arik & Pfister 2021, TabNet

candidates.claim: TabNet outperforms other neural and decision-tree models on a range of tabular benchmarks.

adjudicators.label: Shwartz-Ziv & Armon, tabular data: deep learning is not all you need
Grinsztajn et al., why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on tabular data?

candidates.notes: Tabular baseline case aligned with criterion 5 (XGBoost/TabPFN).

original.label: Ioffe & Szegedy 2015, batch normalization

candidates.claim: Batch normalization speeds training by reducing internal covariate shift.

adjudicators.label: Santurkar et al., how does batch normalization help optimization?

candidates.notes: Performance claim supported; mechanism claim contradicted. Tests claim-level scoring.

original.label: Xu et al. 2019, how powerful are graph neural networks? (GIN)

candidates.claim: GIN is as expressive as the WL test and achieves state-of-the-art graph classification accuracy.

adjudicators.label: Errica et al., a fair comparison of graph neural networks for graph classification

candidates.notes: Expressivity theorem survives; empirical margins shrink under fair evaluation with structure-agnostic baselines. Graph domain matches lab directions.

original.label: Wang et al. 2019, multi-similarity loss for deep metric learning

candidates.claim: The multi-similarity loss improves retrieval accuracy over prior metric-learning losses.

adjudicators.label: Musgrave et al., a metric learning reality check

candidates.notes: Gains largely vanish under fair comparison. Confirm the reality check includes this loss.

original.label: Gulrajani et al. 2017, improved training of Wasserstein GANs

candidates.claim: WGAN-GP gives more stable training and better sample quality than prior GAN objectives.

adjudicators.label: Lucic et al., are GANs created equal?

candidates.notes: With enough tuning budget, objectives reach similar scores. Tuning-budget confound.

original.label: Zoph & Le 2017, neural architecture search with reinforcement learning

candidates.claim: An RL-discovered recurrent cell outperforms LSTM on Penn Treebank language modeling.

adjudicators.label: Melis, Dyer, Blunsom, on the state of the art of evaluation in neural language models

candidates.notes: A well-tuned LSTM outperforms the searched cell. Hyperparameter-budget asymmetry.

original.label: He et al. 2016, deep residual learning

candidates.claim: Residual connections make very deep networks trainable and improve ImageNet accuracy over plain networks of the same depth.

adjudicators.label: He et al., bag of tricks for image classification

candidates.notes: Positive control. Bag of tricks (Amazon) is an independent re-implementation; confirm it re-tests the residual-vs-plain claim rather than only building on ResNet.

original.label: Huang, Kueng, Preskill 2020, predicting many properties of a quantum system from very few measurements (classical shadows)

candidates.claim: Randomized measurements predict M linear functions of an unknown state with sample complexity scaling as log M, independent of system size for local observables.

adjudicators.label: Struchalin et al., experimental estimation of quantum state properties from classical shadows

candidates.notes: Quantum-learning positive with an independent experiment. Check author overlap and whether the experiment tests the scaling claim or one instance.

original.label: Huang et al. 2022, quantum advantage in learning from experiments

candidates.claim: Learning with quantum memory gives an exponential reduction in experiments needed for some tasks, demonstrated on a superconducting processor.
candidates.notes: Positive quantum-advantage claim (sample complexity, not runtime). No independent replication identified; tier C. Theory companions share authors.

original.label: Hensen et al. 2015, loophole-free Bell inequality violation using electron spins

candidates.claim: Bell inequality violation with detection and locality loopholes closed simultaneously.

adjudicators.label: Giustina et al., significant-loophole-free test of Bell's theorem with entangled photons
Shalm et al., strong loophole-free test of local realism

candidates.notes: Three independent groups, different platforms. Positive quantum claim, foundations rather than advantage. Verified overlap: Abellan, Mitchell, Pruneri, Amaya (ICFO) co-author all three tests as suppliers of the random-number generators. Core experimental groups are independent, but the setting-choice component is shared; record it as a common-mode dependency when assigning the tier.

original.label: Google Quantum AI 2024, quantum error correction below the surface code threshold

candidates.claim: Logical error decreases by a factor of about 2 per code-distance step (3 to 5 to 7) on superconducting qubits.
candidates.notes: Positive QEC claim, no independent replication identified on another platform for the same claim. Tier C until one is found.

original.label: Bluvstein et al. 2024, logical quantum processor based on reconfigurable atom arrays

candidates.claim: Neutral-atom arrays run algorithms on up to 48 logical qubits with error-detecting codes, with logical performance improving over physical.
candidates.notes: Neutral-atom positive, relevant to the Q-Factor track. No independent replication identified; tier C.

original.label: Bernien et al. 2017, probing many-body dynamics on a 51-atom quantum simulator

candidates.claim: Rydberg-atom arrays show persistent revivals from a Neel-like state, contrary to expected fast thermalization.

adjudicators.label: Turner et al., weak ergodicity breaking from quantum many-body scars

candidates.notes: Observation reported as an anomaly, explained later by independent theory. Calibration case: the original evidence supports the observation, not a mechanism. Neutral-atom relevant.

original.label: LIGO/Virgo 2016, observation of gravitational waves from a binary black hole merger (GW150914)

adjudicators.label: Nitz et al., 1-OGC: the first open gravitational-wave catalog

original.label: Jumper et al. 2021, highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold

candidates.claim: AlphaFold predicts protein structures with atomic accuracy competitive with experiment in most cases.

original.label: Vaswani et al. 2017, attention is all you need

candidates.claim: A pure-attention encoder-decoder reaches state-of-the-art BLEU on WMT14 En-De and En-Fr at lower training cost.

adjudicators.label: Ott et al., scaling neural machine translation

original.label: Devlin et al. 2019, BERT

candidates.claim: Masked-language-model pretraining followed by fine-tuning sets state of the art on GLUE, SQuAD and other benchmarks.

adjudicators.label: Liu et al., RoBERTa: a robustly optimized BERT pretraining approach

original.label: Kaplan et al. 2020, scaling laws for neural language models

candidates.claim: Loss follows power laws in parameters, data and compute; compute-optimal training favors much larger models trained on relatively less data.

adjudicators.label: Hoffmann et al., training compute-optimal large language models (Chinchilla)

candidates.notes: Power-law form supported; the compute-optimal allocation revised (parameters and tokens scale about equally).
